title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Local scope correctness across the board
summary: Fixes local-scope handling across six providers, adds a declaration-to-usages jump, corrects code lens behavior, and improves const-val folding performance.

highlights.title: Local Scope Correctness
highlights.description: Rename, hover, references, and definitions now distinguish local variables and parameters from workspace-wide symbols — preventing accidental project-wide rewrites when renaming a local and eliminating wrong hover information.

highlights.title: Declaration-to-Usages Jump
highlights.description: Triggering Go to Definition on a local val, var, parameter, for-loop variable, or lambda binding now navigates directly to its usage(s) rather than returning no result.

highlights.title: Code Lens Reliability
highlights.description: Usage counts now appear on interface and abstract method lenses (matching IntelliJ behavior), the smartNavigation setting is respected on single-result clicks, and smart-nav off correctly opens Peek References.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Rename and hover providers now recognize local variables and parameters, preventing workspace-wide symbol rewrites when renaming a local and showing accurate hover information.
Go to Definition on a plain string literal or comment text no longer returns a spurious result.
Named-argument left-hand sides (e.g., `name =` in a function call) now resolve to the correct parameter declaration.
Navigation history Back command preserves the cursor column; Forward remains available after navigating across files.
The const-val folding provider no longer folds the identifier on the declaration line of a val or var.

sections.heading: Improvements
bullets: Const-val folding decorations are now cached by document version and lookups are memoized, eliminating scroll lag on large files.
Local scope resolution now checks function parameters and block-level bindings before falling back to the workspace index, improving definition accuracy throughout.
